mechanism: There are two key-expansion functions and only one of them knows about musig(). %DESC-KEY-PUBKEY-AT (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:556) dispatches to %MUSIG-KEY-PUBKEY-AT at :564 when DESC-KEY-MUSIG-PARTICIPANTS is set; %DESC-KEY-PUBKEY-AT-CACHED (:1687), the wallet/DescriptorCache path behind OUT-DESC-EXPAND-FROM-CACHE and OUT-DESC-EXPAND-WITH-PROVIDER, has no such branch even though its own docstring says to keep the two in sync. A musig desc-key carries NIL in the EXTKEY slot, so it falls into the final cond arm at :1731-1738, and the two shapes fail differently: with NO derivation suffix the path list is empty and DERIVE is :NONE, so FINAL stays NIL, nothing signals inside the handler-case, and the raw (bl.crypto:ext-key-public-bytes NIL) at src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:1752 -- OUTSIDE the handler-case -- raises an unhandled TYPE-ERROR; with a /0/* suffix (bl.crypto:bip32-derive-child NIL ...) signals inside the handler-case and is converted to DESCRIPTOR-DERIVATION-ERROR by the catch-all at :1740. Core has no such split: MuSigPubkeyProvider is an ordinary PubkeyProvider (refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:597) whose GetPubKey (:633) takes read_cache and write_cache and passes them straight through to the participant providers and to the cached aggregate provider, so Expand and ExpandFromCache work on musig exactly as on BIP32. Refuter checks that FAILED to refute it: (1) it is not that musig is unimplemented -- the plain path expands correctly and tests/wallet/descriptor-tests.lisp:1172 pins our musig() output against Core's own vectors, and getdescriptorinfo/deriveaddresses answer normally; (2) it is not a missing-private-key situation -- the ranged form fails IDENTICALLY when the descriptor carries both xprvs, which is what makes the -4 message actively wrong; (3) the TYPE-ERROR is not contained by the import machinery -- %PROCESS-DESCRIPTOR-IMPORT's handler-case (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2179ff) catches only bl.rpc:rpc-error, so a TYPE-ERROR escapes the per-request result and aborts the whole importdescriptors call, reaching the HTTP layer's generic (error (e) ...) at src/rpc/server.lisp:1151 as HTTP 500 with JSON-RPC -32603 "Internal error".
consequence: S2: a valid descriptor that our own getdescriptorinfo calls valid and solvable, and that our own deriveaddresses derives addresses for, cannot be imported into a wallet -- and the two failure modes are both misleading. tr(musig(tpubA,tpubB)) (no derivation) makes importdescriptors raise an unhandled Lisp TYPE-ERROR that surfaces over HTTP as a 500 / "Internal error", i.e. the node reports an internal fault for a well-formed request. tr(musig(tpubA,tpubB)/0/*) makes it return -4 "Cannot expand descriptor. Probably because of hardened derivations without private keys provided", which names a cause that does not apply: the descriptor has no hardened step, and the failure is unchanged when the descriptor supplies both xprvs. An operator following that message hunts for private keys that are already there. The consequence stops short of funds: musig2 signing (nonce exchange, partial signatures) is not implemented in our signer at all -- src/wallet/psbt.lisp only READS the PSBT_IN_MUSIG2_* fields for decodepsbt -- so a successful import could at best have produced a watch-only wallet, and no funds are currently trackable-then-stuck. What is lost is the ability to watch a musig output at all, plus a wrong diagnosis and a 500 on a public RPC surface.
evidence: Container run (bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, warm image, libsecp256k1 with the musig module) on branch fix/ga11v-descriptors-s2; RPCs through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method on a regtest with-wallet-chain-node with both a hot and a watch-only wallet; participant keys derived from fixed seeds (tpubD6NzVbkrYhZ4WVChJhd6GCa8JVfCRQsU9XCgHZNLcnMW4WdJUwCacbLiuXSsPaXZcPmc6LGPxBdkZnCKiLwLJj2q6BQWgSj2JKHF7SM8ivt and tpubD6NzVbkrYhZ4X92z8x8vQMAWpC2FGPTqagpCsFqu8tRZP8GPY5w7iDRFiUiAwF4h5vHdcgGszun56gqPf3zm4ykVaGaMSdxggdkTxETEMMw). FLAT tr(musig(A,B)): getdescriptorinfo -> descriptor echoed with checksum lasdhx8e, isrange false, issolvable T; deriveaddresses -> ("bcrt1p5ycxshedakles8y86vglr3djgypts7xvp4c33m6gezk5mxsw0feq27a9uz"); out-desc-expand -> 5120a130685f2dedbf981c87d311f1c5b24102b878cc0d7118ef48c8ad4d9a0e7a72; out-desc-expand-with-provider with a fresh make-descriptor-cache -> TYPE-ERROR "The value NIL is not of type BITCOIN-LISP.CRYPTO:EXT-KEY"; importdescriptors -> the SAME uncaught TYPE-ERROR (not an rpc-error). RANGED tr(musig(A,B)/0/*): getdescriptorinfo -> valid, isrange T, issolvable T; deriveaddresses [0,1] -> two bcrt1p addresses; out-desc-expand -> 5120a006b79be2b8e87ce5f17269f36992493922dba711edf820cdb916441d53afad; out-desc-expand-with-provider -> BITCOIN-LISP.RPC:DESCRIPTOR-DERIVATION-ERROR; importdescriptors -> (("success" . false) ("error" ("code" . -4) ("message" . "Cannot expand descriptor. Probably because of hardened derivations without private keys provided"))). RANGED WITH BOTH XPRVS tr(musig(tprvA,tprvB)/0/*): getdescriptorinfo reports hasprivatekeys T -- and out-desc-expand-with-provider and importdescriptors fail identically, proving the -4 message wrong. Control tr(tpubA/0/*) in the same run: out-desc-expand-with-provider returned the script plus 1 pubkey and importdescriptors returned (("success" . T)), so the fixture and the cache are sound. Files: src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:556,564,1687,1731-1740,1752,1753-1799; src/wallet/wallet.lisp:2179ff; src/rpc/server.lisp:1151-1158; src/wallet/psbt.lisp:311-373; tests/wallet/descriptor-tests.lisp:1172; refs/bitcoin/src/script/descriptor.cpp:597,633-700.
fix_shape: Give %DESC-KEY-PUBKEY-AT-CACHED the musig branch its sibling already has, shaped like Core's MuSigPubkeyProvider::GetPubKey (descriptor.cpp:633-700) rather than like a copy of %MUSIG-KEY-PUBKEY-AT. At the head of the function, after the const-pubkey short-circuit, test DESC-KEY-MUSIG-PARTICIPANTS: resolve each participant by recursing into %DESC-KEY-PUBKEY-AT-CACHED with the SAME read-cache, write-cache and privkey-provider (Core threads both caches into the participant providers), at position 0 when the participants are unranged and at POS when they are ranged; sort and aggregate exactly as %MUSIG-KEY-PUBKEY-AT does (BIP328 ordering, src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:535-554); then, if the musig key has no path and DERIVE is :NONE, return the aggregate directly, and otherwise build the synthetic xpub root (%MUSIG-SYNTHETIC-XPUB) and walk the path/range through the ordinary BIP32 arm so that PARENT / LAST-HARDENED / DERIVED land in WRITE-CACHE under this key expression's index -- Core caches the aggregate provider's derivation the same way. Factor the shared aggregate-and-derive body out of %MUSIG-KEY-PUBKEY-AT so the two entry points cannot drift again, which is what the :1694 docstring already asks for. Independently of musig, make the crash impossible: the (bl.crypto:ext-key-public-bytes final) at :1752 must be inside the handler-case, or guarded by (unless final (error 'descriptor-derivation-error)), so no key expression the cached path does not understand can ever leave a raw TYPE-ERROR on an RPC surface. Cover it with an importdescriptors test for both the flat and the ranged musig shapes plus a non-musig control, and a unit test asserting OUT-DESC-EXPAND and OUT-DESC-EXPAND-WITH-PROVIDER return the SAME script for every descriptor in the musig Core-vector set.
